content: The studies reviewed various analgesic methods for pain management during labor, comparing different drugs and techniques. 1. Intermittent Auscultation (IA) of Fetal Heart Rate: A study by Martis et al. (2017) assessed the impact of IA on fetal well-being during labor. The evidence quality was rated as very low due to small sample sizes, wide confidence intervals crossing the line of no effect, and inclusion of high-risk pregnancies. The findings suggested a reduction of 3 cases per 1,000 (ranging from 19 fewer to 37 more cases), but the certainty of this effect was very low. 2. Epidural Analgesia vs. No Analgesia: A Cochrane review by Anim-Somuah et al. (2011) compared epidural analgesia with no analgesia or placebo. The evidence was of moderate certainty, showing 45 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 8 fewer to 64 fewer). This was updated for WHO guidelines on intrapartum care. 3. Epidural vs. Parenteral Opioid Analgesia: The same review found moderate-certainty evidence that epidural analgesia resulted in 79 more cases per 1,000 (moderate certainty). However, the confidence intervals were wide, and the sample sizes were small. 4. Pethidine (IM) vs. Placebo: Ullman et al. (2010) reviewed the use of intramuscular pethidine compared to placebo. The evidence was of very low certainty, with 120 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 187 more to 206 fewer). The findings were limited by small sample sizes and wide confidence intervals. 5. Tramadol (IM) vs. No Analgesia: Tramadol was associated with 23 more cases per 1,000 (very low certainty). The evidence was derived from a single study with a moderate risk of bias and wide confidence intervals. 6. Meptazinol (IM) vs. Pethidine (IM): Meptazinol showed 59 more cases per 1,000 (moderate certainty), with confidence intervals ranging from 14 more to 112 more. The evidence was updated for WHO guidelines. 7. Morphine or Diamorphine (IM) vs. Pethidine (IM): Moderate-certainty evidence suggested 12 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 67 more to 73 fewer). The findings were based on a single study with a moderate risk of bias. 8. Patient-Controlled Analgesia (PCA) Pentazocine vs. PCA Pethidine: The evidence was very low, with no estimable effect due to small sample sizes and wide confidence intervals. 9. PCA Remifentanil vs. PCA Pethidine: Low-certainty evidence suggested 19 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 152 fewer to 191 more). The findings were limited by small sample sizes and moderate risk of bias. 10. PCA Nalbuphine vs. PCA Pethidine: Very low-certainty evidence indicated 25 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 43 fewer to 381 more). The findings were derived from a single study with a moderate risk of bias. 11. PCA Fentanyl vs. PCA Pethidine: Low-certainty evidence suggested 51 more cases per 1,000 (ranging from 95 higher to 95 lower). The findings were limited by small sample sizes and wide confidence intervals. 12. Fentanyl (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): Very low-certainty evidence suggested 11 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 17 fewer to 145 more). The findings were based on a single study with a moderate risk of bias. 13. Nalbuphine (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): The evidence was very low, with no estimable effect due to small sample sizes and no events reported. 14. Phenazocine (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): Low-certainty evidence suggested 145 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 52 fewer to 190 fewer). The findings were based on a single study with a moderate risk of bias. 15. Butorphanol (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): Very low-certainty evidence suggested no significant difference, with 0 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 8 fewer to 128 more). 16. Morphine (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): Very low-certainty evidence indicated no estimable effect due to small sample sizes and no events reported. 17. Alphaprodine (IV) vs. Pethidine (IV): Very low-certainty evidence suggested 38 more cases per 1,000 (ranging from 6 fewer to 138 more). The findings were based on a single study with a moderate risk of bias. 18. PCA Meptazinol (IM) vs. PCA Pethidine (IM): Very low-certainty evidence suggested no significant difference, with 0 fewer cases per 1,000 (ranging from 184 fewer to 1,000 more). 19. PCA Fentanyl vs. PCA Pethidine: Low-certainty evidence suggested 95 more cases per 1,000 (ranging from 95 fewer to 95 higher). The findings were limited by small sample sizes and wide confidence intervals. In summary, the studies reviewed various analgesic options for labor pain management, but many were limited by small sample sizes, wide confidence intervals, and moderate to high risks of bias. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, highlighting the need for further high-quality research in this area.
